issue_context.title: API Proposal: MemoryExtensions.SequenceEqual with IComparer<T>
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @GrabYourPitchForks See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
## Background and Motivation We currently have MemoryExtensions.SequenceEqual overloads that work with spans, but they constrain `T : IEquatable`: ```C# public static bool SequenceEqual(this System.ReadOnlySpan span, System.ReadOnlySpan other) where T : System.IEquatable { throw null; } public static bool SequenceEqual(this System.Span span, System.ReadOnlySpan other) where T : System.IEquatable { throw null; } ``` This means there's no built-in support for using `IEqualityComparer`. It also means APIs like `Enumerable.SequenceEqual` that are unconstrained aren't able to delegate to this in general when provided with array inputs. ## Proposed API ```C# public static class MemoryExtensions { public static bool SequenceEqual(this System.ReadOnlySpan span, System.ReadOnlySpan other, IEqualityComparer? comparer); public static bool SequenceEqual(this System.Span span, System.ReadOnlySpan other, IEqualityComparer? comparer); ... } ``` We could also consider doing the same thing for SequenceCompareTo, taking the existing overloads and adding new ones that remove the constraint and accept a nullable `IComparer`. ## Usage Examples For example, we would change `Enumerable.SequenceEqual` to do: ```C# if (first is TSource[] firstArray && second is TSource[] secondArray) { return ((ReadOnlySequence)firstArray).SequenceEqual(secondArray, comparer); }
